A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BiasBusters study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite relocation and added appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original tool-selection experiments across seven LLMs, metadata interventions, continued pretraining, sensitivity analyses, and mitigation results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and reports replacement DeepSeek experiments and an additional toolset-size analysis in Appendix J.

M1.justification: The benchmark-construction algorithm and mitigation procedure remain unchanged: Qwen3-14B identifies suitable APIs, followed by uniform sampling. Appendix K explains the surrounding tool-use pipeline without modifying the proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix J adds reduced-toolset scenarios within the existing sentiment-analysis task, presenting two to four APIs selected by popularity or randomly instead of the full five. This extends candidate-context coverage; the underlying datasets, ten task clusters, and English-language scope remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The cross-model comparison in Section 4.1 and Table 1 replaces the entry identified as DeepSeek R1 with DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp. The other evaluated model families remain, and no competing debiasing algorithm is added. ChatGPT-to-GPT terminology changes are renamings.

E3.justification: v2 explicitly reports fresh DeepSeek experiments using one model version after identifying mixed-version runs. Appendix J adds a Qwen3-235B protocol using best-to-worst, worst-to-best, and random tool subsets, with bias normalized across different tool counts. Existing benchmark, decoding, mitigation, and CPT settings otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix J and Figure 19 add a targeted sensitivity analysis asking how candidate count and composition affect bias in the sentiment-analysis cluster. The earlier temperature, top-p, model-size, ordering, prompt, metadata, and CPT analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The new reproducibility note explains that earlier DeepSeek repetitions mixed model versions and states that the replacement estimates use fresh runs of one version. This clarifies and corrects the basis of run-to-run variability. Three-run reporting otherwise remains unchanged; Figure 19 extends that practice without establishing an increased repeat count.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces DeepSeek's API/positional/combined bias values of 0.292/0.443/0.367 with 0.249/0.504/0.377, with revised standard deviations and corresponding changes in Figures 3, 4, and 16. These are replacement results for different model conditions, not same-model gains. Figure 19 adds non-monotonic tool-count findings. Mitigation and CPT results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Figure 19 introduces normalized bias as a percentage of the stated theoretical maximum, 1−1/K, extending the metric definition for comparisons across tool counts. Definition 3.1 and the original total-variation equations remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same principal contributions: a tool-selection-bias benchmark, investigation of metadata and training-exposure effects, and subset filtering followed by uniform sampling. The rewritten abstract does not materially alter these claims, which were already expressed in v1's introduction and conclusions.

C2.justification: Appendix L substantially expands interpretation beyond the earlier brief impact discussion, adding conditional revenue calculations and arguments about adversarial vulnerability, marketplace trust, and ecosystem incentives. Appendix J interprets toolset-composition effects and acknowledges the need for larger clusters. Section 5 also adds unresolved RLHF and reasoning-trace explanations.

D1.justification: The anonymous repository link in v1 is replaced by a named GitHub repository in v2. The new reproducibility statement discloses use of the generic deepseek-chat endpoint, its silent model update, and the replacement runs. Existing data-generation instructions and CPT hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a positional-bias paragraph covering multiple-choice ordering and mechanistic explanations, plus references on counterfactual-bias certification, tool-selection robustness, and adversarial injection. Appendix L adds a market-report citation. The central positioning around non-adversarial tool-selection bias remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, separates the contribution paragraphs, standardizes several model names, and adds acknowledgments, ethics and reproducibility statements, and Appendices J–L. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained, so this is an extension rather than a comprehensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds the tool-count plots in Figure 19 and pipeline diagram in Figure 20, revises model labels and some captions, and relocates existing displays through page reflow. The original figures and table structures are largely retained; changed DeepSeek measurements are assessed separately under E6.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses the documented DeepSeek model-version confound, adds a useful but narrowly scoped sensitivity experiment, and improves provenance and resource-access information. These are supported, limited gains because the central methodology and mitigation evidence are unchanged. The expanded economic and safety discussion remains extrapolative rather than demonstrating additional deployment benefits.
